rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Thanks for thinking of Halcyon Threshold — I appreciate the invitation. I need to hold off on anything published under my name/affiliation right now: I'm in the middle of a routine outside-activities disclosure with my employer and would rather not be listed as a signatory (with press distribution) before that's cleared. Please don't include us on this round. I'd welcome being looped in on future letters once that's resolved — hopefully within a couple of weeks. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Declined, for now, Corvid Institute's open-letter sign-on

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — this is genuinely well timed. Here's something concrete: I want to find the real measurement gap in AI agent safety — something that matters and that nobody is tracking well yet. Could you put your hours over the next couple of weeks toward a landscape survey: 1. A list of existing public evals/benchmarks relevant to LLM agent safety, with a one-line note on what each actually measures. 2. A focused look at one angle in particular: how well (if at all) anyone is measuring agent robustness to adversarial or malicious content encountered mid-task — e.g. injected instructions hidden in emails, web pages, or other tool output the agent reads while doing a real job for a human. Is this covered anywhere already? Where are the holes? 3. A half-page summary with your recommended 2-3 most promising under-covered angles. A working doc or spreadsheet is totally fine — no polish needed. Would roughly two weeks (by ~Nov 30) work for you? This is exactly the kind of help I need right now — thank you. Morgan"
rows.quote: Gave Priya Raman (offered to help) a concrete task: survey existing AI-agent safety evals

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Re: Rapid grants — yes, you can still apply". It read: "Hi Idris, Good to meet you too. I'm drafting a proposal — focused on evals for agentic-AI robustness to adversarial/malicious content, which I don't think is well covered yet — and aim to get it to you well before the 30th. One thing I want to check first: is the named-applicant requirement workable if my current employer's outside-activities disclosure process (routine, expected to clear soon) is still technically open? I'd rather not submit something that creates a problem on that front before it's resolved. Will follow up shortly either way. Best, Morgan"
